_meta.indication: TEPEZZA is indicated for the treatment of Thyroid Eye Disease.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group study of teprotumumab or placebo (10 mg/kg first infusion, 20 mg/kg subsequent Q3W IV infusions); 24-week treatment followed by 48-week follow-up.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Active Thyroid Eye Disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Overall responder rate in the study eye at Week 24: >=2 mm reduction in proptosis and a >=2-point reduction in clinical activity score (CAS), without deterioration in the non-study eye.
pivotal_trials.result: Proptosis Response Rate 30/42 (71.3%) teprotumumab vs 9/45 (20.0%) placebo, difference 51.1% (95% CI 32.5%, 69.7%); Overall Response Rate 29/42 (69.1%) vs 9/45 (20.0%), difference 48.9% (95% CI 30.2%, 67.6%).

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-masked, placebo-controlled, parallel-group, multicenter study of IV teprotumumab every 3 weeks (Q3W); included a 24-Week Treatment Period and a 48-week follow-up.
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with Active Thyroid Eye Disease
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Proptosis responder rate at Week 24: percentage of subjects with a >=2 mm reduction from baseline in proptosis in the study eye, without deterioration (>=2 mm increase) of proptosis in the fellow eye.
pivotal_trials.result: Proptosis Response Rate 34/41 (82.9%) teprotumumab vs 4/42 (9.5%) placebo, difference 73.4% (95% CI 58.9%, 87.9%); Overall Response Rate 32/41 (78.1%) vs 3/42 (7.1%), difference 70.9% (95% CI 56.0%, 85.8%).

nct_ctgov.title: Treatment of Graves' Orbitopathy (Thyroid Eye Disease) to Reduce Proptosis With Teprotumumab Infusions in a Randomized, Placebo-Controlled, Clinical Study

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>=5%) in the TEPEZZA (N=84) vs placebo (N=86) groups: muscle spasms 25% vs 7%, nausea 17% vs 9%, alopecia 13% vs 8%, diarrhea 12% vs 8%, fatigue 12% vs 7%, hyperglycemia 10% vs 1%, hearing impairment 10% vs 0. Infusion reactions were reported in approximately 4% of patients.
target_moa: Teprotumumab-trbw is a recombinant human IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody that binds to the alpha-subunit of the insulin-like growth factor-1 receptor (IGF-1R) and inhibits the ligand-receptor binding interaction between IGF-1/IGF-2 and IGF-1R.
modality: mAb (fully human IgG1 kappa monoclonal antibody)

rems.type: There are no recommended post-marketing risk evaluation and management strategies (i.e., REMS) for this drug product.

advisory_committee.vote: The Dermatologic and Ophthalmic Drugs Advisory Committee (DODAC) met December 13, 2019 and unanimously voted 'Yes' that the potential benefits of teprotumumab outweigh the potential risks for the intended population.

citations.quote: Teprotumumab was granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of Active Thyroid Eye Disease (Orphan Drug Designation 12-3878). Submission of a pediatric assessment is not required for an application to market a product for an orphan-designated indication. In addition, Thyroid Eye Disease occurs very rarely, if at all in pediatric patients.

summary.text: Teprotumumab was granted Fast Track (April 2015), Breakthrough Therapy (July 2016), and Orphan Drug (June 19, 2019) designations by the FDA for Active Thyroid Eye Disease. The BLA was received July 8, 2019 and reviewed with a March 8, 2020 PDUFA goal date; a DODAC advisory committee met December 13, 2019 and unanimously voted 'Yes' on the benefit-risk. Approval was based on two randomized placebo-controlled studies (Phase 2 TED01RV and Phase 3 HZNP-TEP-301) demonstrating reduction in proptosis; no accelerated approval or REMS was required.

citations.quote: Teprotumumab has been granted Fast Track, Breakthrough Therapy, and Orphan Drug designations by the FDA for the proposed indication, Active Thyroid Eye Disease.

Efficacy with teprotumumab, as demonstrated by a reduction in proptosis, has been demonstrated in two adequate and well controlled studies. The submitted studies are limited in size with only 120 thyroid patients being treated to date.

The committee unanimously voted “Yes”, that the potential benefits of using teprotumumab as recommended outweigh the potential risks associated with the use of the drug product for the intended population.
